A place I visited for a group gathering with friends. What sets it apart from other pork specialty restaurants is the variety of side dishes, sauces, and seasonings.

In the case of pork belly, it is seasoned with various herbs, and in the case of pork neck, it is grilled after spreading butter on the grill. Sauces are provided that can be eaten in various combinations with the meat, including salted fish, salted cutlassfish, ssamjang, red pepper seeds, and wasabi.

A variety of side dishes are provided, including myeongnamul, garlic sprouts, and green onion salad. What is unique is that there are no types of ssam at all. The quality of the meat was good and it was delicious.

If you want a proper “eat like a local” lunch in Gangnam, this buffet is truly the best choice. It's popular among Korean office workers, so it's already guaranteed to be quick, cheap, and delicious. The menu changes regularly so you never get tired of it, and there is always a generous selection of home-style Korean food with plenty of vegetables, so you can fill your plate however you like.

For 10,000 won (about $6.92), you get unlimited drink refills, which is an amazing benefit considering it's near COEX Mall. I went with the intention of having a quick meal, but I ended up feeling much fuller than I expected. All the food was well seasoned and well balanced, so there was nothing greasy or overpowering.

The service was quick and friendly, and the overall atmosphere was unpretentious and comfortable, which was even better. This is the kind of place you'll come back to whenever you want a hearty and delicious lunch without having to worry about where to eat. I would 100% visit again.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
20250517 I used the Six Hands Afternoon Tea Set around 4:30 PM.
Employee service training is required. Not long after the first dish was set, a woman came and cleaned up the empty dishes without asking for understanding. I put it in the last photo. I was eating and there was a tomato pie in my bowl. When I told the server that the meal wasn't over yet, he said that since he was already cleaning up the dishes, he would clean up all but the bowl with the tomato pie on it. It was an embarrassing response, but I asked the server to clean up the dishes after the meal, and the server just put the empty dishes down and walked away without saying sorry. It was shocking and inappropriate service. I didn't want to make a complaint in a good place, and it went smoothly, but I didn't feel good.
First, there was a crispy cylinder with aspic jelly and chamnamul cream cheese, fish mousse, green grape tart, tomato tart, and Korean beef tartare on top of potato gratin. The jelly tasted like Korean food soup made into salty, cool jelly, and it was unique. The crispy cylinder was crispy, but the cheese was too salty. The rest was mediocre.
The lotus tea had a whole lotus flower in it, and it was very pretty. The lotus-shaped dessert was also delicious. Schisandra chinensis tea was so sour that it felt like it refreshed my mouth after eating only sweets. The view from the 24th floor was great and the desserts were pretty and unique.
The third dessert was a caramel tart with yuzu sorbet, matcha, and grapefruit. The yuzu sorbet was extremely sour, but it was like sweet rain in the blood sugar. I would have eaten the dessert with matcha and grapefruit if I could, but it was so tasteless that I left it. The caramel tart was one of the most delicious desserts. It was coated with sugar on top, which made it crunchy and fun to eat, and the flavors of caramel, chocolate, and vanilla were in perfect harmony.
Overall, it was too sweet and I felt a carbohydrate and blood sugar spike, so I asked for some of the desserts to be packaged, and I was glad they did.
Lastly, we had Black Forest with cherries, Baumkuchen with raspberries, and Gugelhof with guava. The cherry jam in Black Forest was too sour and had to be broken open to eat because of the columnar chocolate coating, but the bowl was so small that all the chocolate ended up on the table and it was difficult to eat cleanly. I chose the wrong bowl. The taste wasn't good and the last course was all disappointing. Baumkuchen with raspberries was sour strawberries, a simmering convenience store castella-like bread, and whipped cream. It was a very greasy combination and difficult to eat. The gugelhof with guava was dry. The second course was the best. I hope the service and taste improve. I had a good time.

reviews.author: john Dejong
reviews.text:
Enjoy a 6-course Korean meal + wine pairing at The Lounge on the 24th floor of the Park Hyatt Hotel, located immediately after exiting exit 2 of Samseong Station.
I visited because it was on sale until early June at a reasonable price.
I made a reservation for the city view and expected a view of the colorful neon signs of the city, but maybe because it was too early... there wasn't much to see.
Fortunately, it was raining that day, so there was a bit of charm.
Vegetable sticks and ssam vegetables with dipping sauce as starters, tofu fish, pork maekjeok, flounder, steamed sea bream, grilled Korean beef sirloin as the main, and pot rice with octopus and wild vegetables as a meal...
I was able to enjoy the taste and style of Korean dining.
It's not a high-end wine, but a glass each of champagne, white wine, and red wine.
When I drank it with food, I got moderately drunk and it was nice.
However, due to the nature of the lounge, the tables are very open and face the indoor pool with one window.
The luxurious feel is a bit lacking due to the noise from the pool and the occasional sight of people wearing only swimsuits coming and going.
Also, the bathroom was downstairs, so it was a little inconvenient to have to take the elevator down.
